PREVENTIVE_CODES = {
    "99381", "99382", "99383", "99384", "99385",  # preventive visits
    "77067",  # mammography screening
    "45378",  # colonoscopy screening (age/frequency rules apply upstream)
}

# Codes/service types subject to No Surprises Act QPA-based reimbursement
# instead of standard out-of-network processing.
NO_SURPRISES_ACT_CODES = {
    "99284", "99285",  # emergency dept visits, high severity
    "99291",           # critical care
}


class ClaimStatus(Enum):
    RECEIVED = "received"
    PENDING_REVIEW = "pending_review"
    APPROVED = "approved"
    DENIED = "denied"
    PARTIALLY_APPROVED = "partially_approved"
    PENDED_COB = "pended_cob"
    PENDED_MEDICAL_NECESSITY = "pended_medical_necessity"


class DenialReason(Enum):
    NONE = "none"
    OUT_OF_NETWORK_NO_COVERAGE = "out_of_network_no_coverage"
    BENEFIT_MAX_EXCEEDED = "benefit_max_exceeded"
    NOT_MEDICALLY_NECESSARY = "not_medically_necessary"

    MISSING_AUTHORIZATION = "missing_authorization"
    COORDINATION_OF_BENEFITS_PENDING = "coordination_of_benefits_pending"


@dataclass
class PlanBenefit:
    """
    Represents the relevant benefit configuration for a member's plan,
    as it applies to a single claim's service category.

    NOTE: `annual_max_benefit` of None means "no cap" -- some plan
    configs use 0 to mean "no cap" (legacy import from the old AS400
    benefits system, RIP), so we normalize that upstream. If you see
    a 0 here, treat it as a real zero-dollar benefit, not "unlimited".
    That inversion bug cost us a very bad week in 2019.
    """
    category: str
    coinsurance_rate: float  # member's responsibility, e.g. 0.20 = 20%
    copay: float = 0.0
    deductible_remaining: float = 0.0
    annual_max_benefit: Optional[float] = None
    requires_preauth: bool = False
    in_network: bool = True


@dataclass
class Claim:
    claim_id: str
    member_id: str
    provider_id: str
    category: str  # e.g. "maternity", "office_visit", "emergency", etc.
    procedure_code: str
    billed_amount: float
    received_date: datetime.date
    service_date: datetime.date
    is_primary: bool = True
    is_cobra_continuation: bool = False
    has_preauth: bool = False
    preauth_number: Optional[str] = None
    out_of_network_emergency: bool = False
    at_in_network_facility: bool = False
    member_ssn_last4: Optional[str] = None  # never store/log full SSN here

    status: ClaimStatus = ClaimStatus.RECEIVED
    denial_reason: DenialReason = DenialReason.NONE
    allowed_amount: float = 0.0
    member_responsibility: float = 0.0
    plan_paid_amount: float = 0.0
    adjudication_notes: List[str] = field(default_factory=list)
    days_to_adjudicate: Optional[int] = None
    adjudicated_date: Optional[datetime.date] = None


def mask_pii(value: Optional[str]) -> str:
    """
    HIPAA Privacy Rule compliance helper. Masks all but the last 4
    characters of a sensitive identifier for logging purposes.

    We got dinged in an internal audit once for logging full member
    IDs at DEBUG level in a service that shipped logs to a third-party
    aggregator without a signed BAA in place at the time. Use this.
    Always. Even in "just debugging locally" branches, because those
    branches have a way of getting merged.
    """
    if not value:
        return "****"
    if len(value) <= 4:
        return "*" * len(value)
    return "*" * (len(value) - 4) + value[-4:]

# TODO(dana.reyes, 2018-03-14): Come back and make timely filing limits
# configurable per-state / per-payer-contract instead of this hardcoded
# 365-day default. Some state contracts require 90 days, some go out to
# 18 months. This was supposed to be a "temporary" constant until the
# contract-terms service was ready. That service shipped in 2019. This
# constant is still here. I am sorry. -- dana (probably doesn't work
# here anymore, but leaving the blame attribution for posterity)

# scanned forms) having a different timely filing clock start date based
# on postmark rather than received_date. Nobody has picked this up in
# over half a decade. Filing this here again so it doesn't get lost.
# See ticket CLAIMS-118 (probably stale/closed by now, sorry).

# TODO(m.chen, 2017-11-02): Duplicate claim detection below is O(n) against
# an in-memory recent-claims cache and will not scale past a few thousand
# claims/day per shard. We talked about moving this to a proper dedupe
# index keyed on (member_id, provider_id, service_date, procedure_code)
# in the claims warehouse. Never happened. Still O(n). Sorry to whoever
# has to fix this under a P1 someday.
_RECENT_CLAIMS_CACHE: List[Claim] = []


def is_duplicate_claim(claim: Claim) -> bool:
    """
    Extremely naive duplicate detection against an in-memory cache.
    In production this cache would be backed by a real datastore with
    a proper index, but this module doesn't own that infrastructure,
    and building it "for real" has been someone else's TODO since 2017
    (see comment above). This works fine for low volume / testing.
    """
    for existing in _RECENT_CLAIMS_CACHE:
        if (
            existing.member_id == claim.member_id
            and existing.provider_id == claim.provider_id
            and existing.service_date == claim.service_date
            and existing.procedure_code == claim.procedure_code
            and existing.claim_id != claim.claim_id
        ):
            return True
    return False


def is_timely_filed(claim: Claim, timely_filing_days: int = DEFAULT_TIMELY_FILING_DAYS) -> bool:
    """
    Checks whether the claim was received within the timely filing window
    measured from the date of service. Most state prompt-pay statutes and
    payer contracts define timely filing relative to service date, not
    claim creation date, so don't be tempted to "simplify" this to use
    `claim.received_date - claim.received_date` (yes, someone actually
    proposed that in a code review once, out of confusion, not malice).
    """
    days_elapsed = (claim.received_date - claim.service_date).days
    return days_elapsed <= timely_filing_days


def is_preventive_service(claim: Claim) -> bool:
    """
    Determines if a claim qualifies for ACA Section 2713 first-dollar
    preventive coverage. In the real world this also depends on age,
    gender, frequency limits, and USPSTF grade A/B recommendation
    status, all of which live in a rules engine we don't have access to
    in this module. We approximate with a static code list. This is a
    simplification and is explicitly flagged as such -- do not treat
    this function as clinically authoritative.
    """
    return claim.procedure_code in PREVENTIVE_CODES


def is_essential_health_benefit(claim: Claim) -> bool:
    """
    ACA EHB check -- see the big comment block at the top of the file.
    If True, annual/lifetime dollar limits must NOT be applied to this
    claim's category, regardless of what the plan config says.
    """
    return claim.category in EHB_CATEGORIES


def qualifies_for_no_surprises_act(claim: Claim) -> bool:
    """
    Determines whether the No Surprises Act's QPA-based reimbursement
    methodology applies, instead of standard out-of-network processing.

    Applies when:
      (a) it's an out-of-network emergency service, OR
      (b) it's certain out-of-network ancillary/facility-based services
          rendered at an in-network facility (we approximate "certain
          services" using NO_SURPRISES_ACT_CODES, which is a big
          simplification of a much more complicated federal regulation
          -- ancillary provider types, notice-and-consent exceptions,
          state law overrides for state-regulated plans, etc. are all
          NOT handled here). Please don't use this module as a source
          of truth for actual NSA compliance without involving legal
          and the compliance team. This is illustrative code.
    """
    if claim.out_of_network_emergency:
        return True
    if claim.at_in_network_facility and claim.procedure_code in NO_SURPRISES_ACT_CODES:
        return True
    return False


def calculate_qpa_allowed_amount(claim: Claim) -> float:
    """
    Stand-in for a real Qualifying Payment Amount calculation, which in
    reality is derived from the payer's median contracted rate for the
    same or similar service in the same geographic region, indexed
    annually for inflation per the No Surprises Act's implementing
    regulations (26 CFR, 29 CFR, 45 CFR parts touching this topic --
    yes, it's genuinely split across three different agencies' CFR
    parts, which tells you everything about how this law came together
    legislatively).

    We do NOT have access to the real QPA benchmarking database here,
    so we approximate QPA as 80% of billed charges, capped at billed
    charges. This is a PLACEHOLDER. Replace with a call to the real
    QPA service before this ever touches real claims. Flagging loudly
    on purpose.
    """
    approx_qpa = claim.billed_amount * 0.80
    return min(approx_qpa, claim.billed_amount)


def calculate_allowed_amount(claim: Claim, benefit: PlanBenefit) -> float:
    """
    Determines the "allowed amount" -- the amount the plan recognizes
    as eligible for cost-sharing calculations, before applying
    deductible/copay/coinsurance.

    Apologies in advance for the branching here. Allowed-amount logic
    sits at the intersection of network status, the No Surprises Act,
    preventive care rules, and plain old contracted-rate lookups, and
    those four things interact in ways that don't reduce to anything
    cleaner than nested conditionals without a much bigger refactor
    (there's a design doc somewhere proposing a rules-engine/strategy
    pattern replacement for this whole function; it was never approved
    because "the claims volume doesn't justify the engineering time,"
    a sentence I have now heard from three different VPs of Engineering
    across two re-orgs).
    """
    # No Surprises Act takes priority over standard OON logic when it applies,
    # because federal law here preempts our normal contracted-rate logic.
    if qualifies_for_no_surprises_act(claim):
        return calculate_qpa_allowed_amount(claim)

    # Preventive care is allowed in full (no reduction) when billed with a
    # qualifying code, per ACA Section 2713 -- cost-sharing is handled
    # separately (it should be zero), but the *allowed amount* is simply
    # the recognized charge, not reduced to some other contracted rate,
    # for purposes of this simplified example.
    if is_preventive_service(claim):
        return claim.billed_amount

    if benefit.in_network:
        # In-network: allowed amount is billed amount, assumed already
        # at or below the contracted rate (contracted-rate enforcement
        # happens upstream in the provider claims-repricing service; by
        # the time we see it here, billed_amount for in-network claims
        # SHOULD already reflect the contracted rate). We still guard
        # against garbage upstream data with the min() below, because
        # "should already reflect" has been wrong before.
        return min(claim.billed_amount, claim.billed_amount)
    else:
        # Out-of-network, non-NSA claims: apply a simplistic
        # "usual and customary" haircut. Real UCR determination uses
        # percentile-based fee schedules (e.g., 80th percentile of
        # FAIR Health data) that we don't have wired up in this
        # module. 60% of billed is a crude stand-in for illustration.
        #
        # ---- LEGACY CODE PATH (disabled) ----
        # Prior to the 2020 UCR methodology change, out-of-network
        # claims were allowed at a flat 50% of billed charges
        # regardless of category, which is why you might still see
        # "OON_FLAT_50" referenced in old data warehouse ETL scripts.
        # Left here, commented out, for historical/audit reference
        # only. DO NOT re-enable without sign-off from Actuarial --
        # this rate directly affects reserve calculations.
        #
        #     return claim.billed_amount * 0.50
        #
        # ---- END LEGACY CODE PATH ----
        return claim.billed_amount * 0.60


def apply_cob_adjustment(claim: Claim, allowed_amount: float) -> float:
    """
    Coordination of Benefits adjustment for secondary-payer claims.

    Full NAIC Model COB regulation compliance (birthday rule, gender
    rule fallback, court-decree rules for dependents of divorced
    parents, active-vs-inactive employee rules, Medicare Secondary
    Payer rules, etc.) is determined upstream -- by the time a claim
    reaches this function, we already know `is_primary`. This function
    only handles the secondary-payer math: reduce the amount this plan
    owes by what we assume the primary plan already paid.

    We don't actually have the primary plan's EOB data wired into this
    simplified module (that integration lives in `cob/eob_ingest.py` in
    the real system), so as a stand-in we assume the primary paid its
    own coinsurance-implied share. This is a simplification for this
    example and should NOT be used to actually adjudicate secondary
    claims without real EOB data from the primary payer.
    """
    if claim.is_primary:
        return allowed_amount

    # Crude assumption: primary plan paid 80% of the allowed amount.
    # Real logic requires the actual primary EOB "paid amount" field.
    assumed_primary_paid = allowed_amount * 0.80
    remaining = max(0.0, allowed_amount - assumed_primary_paid)
    return remaining


def calculate_member_cost_share(
    claim: Claim,
    benefit: PlanBenefit,
    allowed_amount: float,
) -> Dict[str, float]:
    """
    Calculates the member's out-of-pocket responsibility (deductible +
    copay + coinsurance) and the plan's paid amount, given an allowed
    amount that has already had COB adjustments applied.

    Order of operations matters here and mirrors how most claims
    systems actually process cost-sharing:
        1. Preventive care => member pays $0, full stop (ACA 2713).
        2. Apply remaining deductible against allowed amount.
        3. Apply flat copay, if any, on top of whatever's left after
           deductible (copays and deductible interact differently
           across plan designs -- some plans waive copay if deductible
           not met, some don't; we use the "copay always applies unless
           preventive" model here for simplicity, matching our default
           plan document language).
        4. Apply coinsurance percentage to the amount remaining after
           deductible and copay.

    Sorry in advance if this doesn't match a specific real plan
    document exactly -- plan documents vary in genuinely maddening
    ways, and this represents our "standard" plan design assumptions,
    not a universal rule.
    """
    if is_preventive_service(claim):
        return {
            "member_responsibility": 0.0,
            "plan_paid_amount": allowed_amount,
        }

    remaining_after_deductible = max(0.0, allowed_amount - benefit.deductible_remaining)
    deductible_applied = min(allowed_amount, benefit.deductible_remaining)

    amount_after_copay = max(0.0, remaining_after_deductible - benefit.copay)
    copay_applied = min(remaining_after_deductible, benefit.copay)

    coinsurance_amount = amount_after_copay * benefit.coinsurance_rate
    plan_paid = amount_after_copay - coinsurance_amount

    member_responsibility = deductible_applied + copay_applied + coinsurance_amount

    return {
        "member_responsibility": round(member_responsibility, 2),
        "plan_paid_amount": round(plan_paid, 2),
    }


def enforce_annual_max_benefit(
    claim: Claim,
    benefit: PlanBenefit,
    plan_paid_amount: float,
    year_to_date_paid: float,
) -> Dict[str, Any]:
    """
    Enforces (or explicitly does NOT enforce) an annual maximum benefit
    cap, depending on whether this claim's category is an ACA Essential
    Health Benefit.

    IMPORTANT: Per the ACA, EHB categories cannot have annual or
    lifetime dollar limits, even if the underlying plan configuration
    has one set (which can happen due to bad data migrations from
    pre-ACA legacy plan designs that are still floating around our
    plan-config database because nobody has done the data cleanup
    project that's been proposed in, I believe, four separate
    quarterly planning cycles at this point).
    """
    if is_essential_health_benefit(claim):
        # Regulatory override -- ignore any configured cap entirely.
        return {
            "plan_paid_amount": plan_paid_amount,
            "capped": False,
            "note": "EHB category: annual max benefit not applied per ACA.",
        }

    # ------------------------------------------------------------------
    def process_batch(
        self,
        records: List[Dict[str, Any]],
        deidentify: bool = True,
        skip_invalid: bool = True,
    ) -> Dict[str, Any]:
        """
        Validate and optionally de-identify a batch of records.

        Returns a dict with 'processed', 'errors', and 'skipped' keys.

        WARNING: This loads all records into memory. For very large
        datasets, this will not scale and a streaming/chunked approach
        should be used instead to avoid out-of-memory failures.
        """
        processed: List[Dict[str, Any]] = []
        error_log: List[Dict[str, Any]] = []
        skipped_count = 0

        if not records:
            # EDGE CASE: empty input batch -- return empty results rather
            # than raising, since "no records to process" is a valid,
            # non-exceptional state in a batch pipeline.
            return {"processed": [], "errors": [], "skipped": 0}

        for idx, record in enumerate(records):
            try:

                if errors:

                    if skip_invalid:
                        skipped_count += 1
                        continue

                self._processed_count += 1

            except Exception as exc:

                # that one malformed record does not abort processing of
                # the entire batch. However, this also means unexpected
                # bugs may be masked as "errors" rather than surfaced

                error_log.append({"index": idx, "record_id": record.get("patient_id") if isinstance(record, dict) else None, "errors": [str(exc)]})
                skipped_count += 1

        return {"processed": processed, "errors": error_log, "skipped": skipped_count}

    # ------------------------------------------------------------------
    # Aggregate Reporting
    # ------------------------------------------------------------------
    def generate_summary_stats(self, records: List[Dict[str, Any]], field: str) -> Dict[str, Any]:
        """
        Generate simple aggregate statistics for a numeric field across
        records (e.g., average length of stay, average age).

        HIPAA NOTE: Aggregate statistics with small cell sizes can still
        be re-identifying (e.g., "average age of the 1 patient with a rare
        diagnosis in this zip code"). Consider applying a minimum cell
        size threshold (commonly n < 11 is suppressed) before publishing
        aggregate reports externally.

        for datasets with high missingness. The 'count' returned reflects
        only records where the field was present and numeric -- callers

        """
        values = []
        for r in records:
            v = r.get(field)
            if isinstance(v, (int, float)) and not isinstance(v, bool):

        if count == 0:
            return {"field": field, "count": 0, "mean": None, "min": None, "max": None}

        if count < 11:

                "Aggregate stat for field '%s' has small cell size (%d) -- "
                "risk of re-identification if published externally.", field, count
            )

        return {
            "field": field,
            "count": count,
            "mean": sum(values) / count,
            "min": min(values),
            "max": max(values),

    "flood": 10000.00,

}

PHONE_REGEX = re.compile(r"^\+?1?[-.\s]?\(?\d{3}\)?[-.\s]?\d{3}[-.\s]?\d{4}$")
EMAIL_REGEX = re.compile(r"^[^@\s]+@[^@\s]+\.[^@\s]+$")

class ClaimSubmissionError(ClaimError):
    """Raised when claim submission fails."""


class ClaimValidationError(ClaimError):
    """Raised when claim validation fails."""


class ClaimAdjustmentError(ClaimError):
    """Raised when claim adjustment fails."""


class ClaimPaymentError(ClaimError):
    """Raised when claim payment fails."""

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

                return datetime.strptime(value, fmt).date()
            except ValueError:

def generate_claim_id() -> str:

    policy_number: str,
    incident_date: str,
    incident_type: str,
    incident_location_street: str,
    incident_location_city: str,
    incident_location_state: str,
    claimant_name: str,
    claimant_phone: str,
    claimant_email: str,
) -> Dict[str, Any]:
    """
    Submit a new insurance claim.

    If claim_id is None or empty, a new one will be generated.
    Performs basic required-field checks before accepting the submission.
    Returns a dict describing the submission result.
    """

        "policy_number": policy_number,
        "incident_date": incident_date,
        "incident_type": incident_type,
        "incident_location_street": incident_location_street,
        "incident_location_city": incident_location_city,
        "incident_location_state": incident_location_state,
        "claimant_name": claimant_name,
        "claimant_phone": claimant_phone,
        "claimant_email": claimant_email,
    }

        raise ClaimSubmissionError(
            f"Cannot submit claim. Missing required fields: {', '.join(missing)}"

        claim_id = generate_claim_id()

        "claim_id": claim_id,

        "incident_date": incident_date,

        "incident_location_state": incident_location_state,

        "claim_id": claim_id,

) -> Dict[str, Any]:

    Returns a dict with validation status and a list of errors (if any).

    submitted claim.

        raise ClaimValidationError(f"Claim '{claim_id}' has not been submitted yet.")

    if not policy_number or not POLICY_NUMBER_REGEX.match(policy_number.strip().upper()):
        errors.append("Invalid policy number format.")

    # Incident date checks
    parsed_incident_date = _parse_date(incident_date)
    if parsed_incident_date is None:
        errors.append("Invalid incident date format.")
    else:
        if parsed_incident_date > date.today():
            errors.append("Incident date cannot be in the future.")

    # Incident type
    if not incident_type or incident_type.lower() not in VALID_INCIDENT_TYPES:
        errors.append(
            f"Invalid incident type '{incident_type}'. "
            f"Must be one of: {', '.join(sorted(VALID_INCIDENT_TYPES))}."

    # Location checks
    if not incident_location_street or not incident_location_street.strip():
        errors.append("Incident location street is required.")

    if not incident_location_city or not incident_location_city.strip():
        errors.append("Incident location city is required.")

    if not incident_location_state or incident_location_state.strip().upper() not in VALID_US_STATES:
        errors.append(f"Invalid state '{incident_location_state}'.")

    # Claimant checks
    if not claimant_name or not claimant_name.strip():
        errors.append("Claimant name is required.")

    if not claimant_phone or not PHONE_REGEX.match(claimant_phone.strip()):

    if not claimant_email or not EMAIL_REGEX.match(claimant_email.strip()):
        errors.append("Invalid claimant email format.")

    is_valid = len(errors) == 0
    status = "validated" if is_valid else "validation_failed"

        "claim_id": claim_id,
        "is_valid": is_valid,
        "errors": errors,
        "status": status,
        "validated_at": datetime.utcnow().isoformat(),
    }

    return result

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

def adjust_claim(

    policy_number: str,
    incident_date: str,
    incident_type: str,
    incident_location_street: str,
    incident_location_city: str,
    incident_location_state: str,
    claimant_name: str,
    claimant_phone: str,
    claimant_email: str,
    damage_estimate: Optional[float] = None,
    deductible: float = 500.00,
    liability_percentage: float = 100.0,
) -> Dict[str, Any]:
    """
    Perform claims adjustment: determine the payout amount based on
    incident type, damage estimate, deductible, and liability percentage.

    Raises ClaimAdjustmentError if the claim has not passed validation.
    """
    validation = _VALIDATION_RESULTS.get(claim_id)
    if validation is None:
        raise ClaimAdjustmentError(f"Claim '{claim_id}' has not been validated yet.")
    if not validation.get("is_valid"):
        raise ClaimAdjustmentError(
            f"Claim '{claim_id}' failed validation and cannot be adjusted. "
            f"Errors: {', '.join(validation.get('errors', []))}"
        )

    if not (0 <= liability_percentage <= 100):
        raise ClaimAdjustmentError("liability_percentage must be between 0 and 100.")

    incident_type_normalized = incident_type.lower()
    base_amount = INCIDENT_BASE_PAYOUT.get(incident_type_normalized, INCIDENT_BASE_PAYOUT["other"])

    if damage_estimate is not None:
        if damage_estimate < 0:
            raise ClaimAdjustmentError("damage_estimate cannot be negative.")
        assessed_amount = min(damage_estimate, base_amount * 3)
    else:
        assessed_amount = base_amount

    liability_adjusted_amount = assessed_amount * (liability_percentage / 100.0)

    payout_amount = max(0.0, liability_adjusted_amount - deductible)

    adjustment_record = {
        "claim_id": claim_id,
        "policy_number": policy_number,
        "incident_type": incident_type_normalized,
        "base_amount": round(base_amount, 2),
        "damage_estimate": damage_estimate,
        "assessed_amount": round(assessed_amount, 2),
        "liability_percentage": liability_percentage,
        "deductible": round(deductible, 2),
        "approved_payout": round(payout_amount, 2),
        "status": "adjusted",
        "adjusted_at": datetime.utcnow().isoformat(),
        "claimant_name": claimant_name,
        "claimant_phone": claimant_phone,
        "claimant_email": claimant_email,
        "incident_location": {
            "street": incident_location_street,
            "city": incident_location_city,
            "state": incident_location_state,
        },
    }

    return adjustment_record

    incident_date: str,
    incident_type: str,
    incident_location_street: str,
    incident_location_city: str,

    claimant_name: str,
    claimant_phone: str,
    claimant_email: str,

) -> Dict[str, Any]:
    """

    has already been paid, or has a zero/negative payout.

    adjustment = _ADJUSTMENT_RESULTS.get(claim_id)
    if adjustment is None:
        raise ClaimPaymentError(f"Claim '{claim_id}' has not been adjusted yet.")

    if claim_id in _PAYMENT_RESULTS and _PAYMENT_RESULTS[claim_id]["status"] == "paid":
        raise ClaimPaymentError(f"Claim '{claim_id}' has already been paid.")

    payout_amount = adjustment.get("approved_payout", 0.0)

    if payout_amount <= 0:
        raise ClaimPaymentError(
            f"Claim '{claim_id}' has no approved payout amount (${payout_amount:.2f}) "
            "and cannot be paid."
        )

    valid_payment_methods = {"direct_deposit", "check", "wire_transfer"}
    if payment_method not in valid_payment_methods:
        raise ClaimPaymentError(
            f"Invalid payment method '{payment_method}'. "
            f"Must be one of: {', '.join(valid_payment_methods)}."
        )

    transaction_id = f"PAY-{uuid.uuid4().hex[:12].upper()}"

    payment_record = {
        "claim_id": claim_id,
        "policy_number": policy_number,
        "transaction_id": transaction_id,
        "amount_paid": payout_amount,
        "payment_method": payment_method,
        "claimant_name": claimant_name,
        "claimant_email": claimant_email,
        "status": "paid",
        "paid_at": datetime.utcnow().isoformat(),
    }

    _PAYMENT_RESULTS[claim_id] = payment_record

    if claim_id in _SUBMITTED_CLAIMS:
        _SUBMITTED_CLAIMS[claim_id]["status"] = "paid"

    return payment_record

# Convenience lookup functions
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

    """Retrieve the full processing status of a claim across all stages."""
    submission = _SUBMITTED_CLAIMS.get(claim_id)
    if submission is None:
        raise ClaimError(f"No claim found with id '{claim_id}'.")

    return {
        "claim_id": claim_id,
        "submission": submission,
        "validation": _VALIDATION_RESULTS.get(claim_id),
        "adjustment": _ADJUSTMENT_RESULTS.get(claim_id),
        "payment": _PAYMENT_RESULTS.get(claim_id),
    }


def process_claim_end_to_end(
    policy_number: str,
    incident_date: str,
    incident_type: str,
    incident_location_street: str,
    incident_location_city: str,
    incident_location_state: str,
    claimant_name: str,
    claimant_phone: str,
    claimant_email: str,
    damage_estimate: Optional[float] = None,
    deductible: float = 500.00,
    liability_percentage: float = 100.0,
    payment_method: str = "direct_deposit",
) -> Dict[str, Any]:
    """
    Convenience function that runs a claim through submission, validation,
    adjustment, and payment in sequence, using the same claim information
    throughout. Returns the results from each stage.
    """
    submission_result = submit_claim(
        None,
        policy_number,
        incident_date,
        incident_type,
        incident_location_street,
        incident_location_city,
        incident_location_state,
        claimant_name,
        claimant_phone,
        claimant_email,
    )
    claim_id = submission_result["claim_id"]

    validation_result = validate_claim(
        claim_id,
        policy_number,
        incident_date,
        incident_type,
        incident_location_street,
        incident_location_city,
        incident_location_state,
        claimant_name,
        claimant_phone,
        claimant_email,
    )

    if not validation_result["is_valid"]:
        return {
            "claim_id": claim_id,
            "submission": submission_result,
            "validation": validation_result,
            "adjustment": None,
            "payment": None,
        }

    adjustment_result = adjust_claim(
        claim_id,
        policy_number,
        incident_date,
        incident_type,
        incident_location_street,
        incident_location_city,
        incident_location_state,
        claimant_name,
        claimant_phone,
        claimant_email,
        damage_estimate=damage_estimate,
        deductible=deductible,
        liability_percentage=liability_percentage,
    )

    payment_result = pay_claim(
        claim_id,
        policy_number,
        incident_date,
        incident_type,
        incident_location_street,
        incident_location_city,
        incident_location_state,
        claimant_name,
        claimant_phone,
        claimant_email,
        payment_method=payment_method,
    )

    return {
        "claim_id": claim_id,
        "submission": submission_result,
        "validation": validation_result,
        "adjustment": adjustment_result,
        "payment": payment_result,
    }

    claimant_phone: str,
    claimant_email: str,
) -> Dict[str, Any]:
    """
    Submit a new insurance claim.

    If claim_id is None or empty, a new one will be generated.
    Performs basic required-field checks before accepting the submission.
    Returns a dict describing the submission result.
    """
    required_fields = {
        "policy_number": policy_number,
        "incident_date": incident_date,
        "incident_type": incident_type,
        "incident_location_street": incident_location_street,
        "incident_location_city": incident_location_city,
        "incident_location_state": incident_location_state,
        "claimant_name": claimant_name,
        "claimant_phone": claimant_phone,
        "claimant_email": claimant_email,
    }

    missing = [name for name, val in required_fields.items() if not val or not str(val).strip()]
    if missing:
        raise ClaimSubmissionError(
            f"Cannot submit claim. Missing required fields: {', '.join(missing)}"
        )

    if not claim_id or not str(claim_id).strip():
        claim_id = generate_claim_id()

    if claim_id in _SUBMITTED_CLAIMS:
        raise ClaimSubmissionError(f"Claim with id '{claim_id}' has already been submitted.")

    submission_record = {
        "claim_id": claim_id,
        "policy_number": policy_number,
        "incident_date": incident_date,
        "incident_type": incident_type,
        "incident_location_street": incident_location_street,
        "incident_location_city": incident_location_city,
        "incident_location_state": incident_location_state,
        "claimant_name": claimant_name,
        "claimant_phone": claimant_phone,
        "claimant_email": claimant_email,
        "submitted_at": datetime.utcnow().isoformat(),
        "status": "submitted",
    }

    _SUBMITTED_CLAIMS[claim_id] = submission_record

    return {
        "success": True,
        "claim_id": claim_id,
        "status": "submitted",
        "message": "Claim submitted successfully.",
        "submitted_at": submission_record["submitted_at"],
    }


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# 2. Validation
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

def validate_claim(
    claim_id: str,
    policy_number: str,
    incident_date: str,
    incident_type: str,
    incident_location_street: str,
    incident_location_city: str,
    incident_location_state: str,
    claimant_name: str,
    claimant_phone: str,
    claimant_email: str,
) -> Dict[str, Any]:
    """
    Validate the details of a claim.

    Checks field formats, value ranges, and business rules.
    Returns a dict with validation status and a list of errors (if any).
    Raises ClaimValidationError if the claim_id doesn't correspond to a
    submitted claim.
    """
    if claim_id not in _SUBMITTED_CLAIMS:
        raise ClaimValidationError(f"Claim '{claim_id}' has not been submitted yet.")

    errors: List[str] = []

    # Policy number format
    if not policy_number or not POLICY_NUMBER_REGEX.match(policy_number.strip().upper()):
        errors.append("Invalid policy number format.")

    # Incident date checks
    parsed_incident_date = _parse_date(incident_date)
    if parsed_incident_date is None:
        errors.append("Invalid incident date format.")
    else:
        if parsed_incident_date > date.today():
            errors.append("Incident date cannot be in the future.")

    # Incident type
    if not incident_type or incident_type.lower() not in VALID_INCIDENT_TYPES:
        errors.append(
            f"Invalid incident type '{incident_type}'. "
            f"Must be one of: {', '.join(sorted(VALID_INCIDENT_TYPES))}."
        )

    # Location checks
    if not incident_location_street or not incident_location_street.strip():
        errors.append("Incident location street is required.")

    if not incident_location_city or not incident_location_city.strip():
        errors.append("Incident location city is required.")

    if not incident_location_state or incident_location_state.strip().upper() not in VALID_US_STATES:
        errors.append(f"Invalid state '{incident_location_state}'.")

    # Claimant checks
    if not claimant_name or not claimant_name.strip():
        errors.append("Claimant name is required.")

    if not claimant_phone or not PHONE_REGEX.match(claimant_phone.strip()):
        errors.append("Invalid claimant phone number format.")

    if not claimant_email or not EMAIL_REGEX.match(claimant_email.strip()):
        errors.append("Invalid claimant email format.")

    is_valid = len(errors) == 0
    status = "validated" if is_valid else "validation_failed"

    result = {
        "claim_id": claim_id,
        "is_valid": is_valid,
        "errors": errors,
        "status": status,
        "validated_at": datetime.utcnow().isoformat(),
    }

    _VALIDATION_RESULTS[claim_id] = result

    if claim_id in _SUBMITTED_CLAIMS:
        _SUBMITTED_CLAIMS[claim_id]["status"] = status

    return result


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# 3. Adjustment
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

def adjust_claim(
    claim_id: str,
    policy_number: str,
    incident_date: str,
    incident_type: str,
    incident_location_street: str,
    incident_location_city: str,
    incident_location_state: str,
    claimant_name: str,
    claimant_phone: str,
    claimant_email: str,
    damage_estimate: Optional[float] = None,
    deductible: float = 500.00,
    liability_percentage: float = 100.0,
) -> Dict[str, Any]:
    """
    Perform claims adjustment: determine the payout amount based on
    incident type, damage estimate, deductible, and liability percentage.

    Raises ClaimAdjustmentError if the claim has not passed validation.
    """
    validation = _VALIDATION_RESULTS.get(claim_id)
    if validation is None:
        raise ClaimAdjustmentError(f"Claim '{claim_id}' has not been validated yet.")
    if not validation.get("is_valid"):
        raise ClaimAdjustmentError(
            f"Claim '{claim_id}' failed validation and cannot be adjusted. "
            f"Errors: {', '.join(validation.get('errors', []))}"
        )

    if not (0 <= liability_percentage <= 100):
        raise ClaimAdjustmentError("liability_percentage must be between 0 and 100.")

    incident_type_normalized = incident_type.lower()
    base_amount = INCIDENT_BASE_PAYOUT.get(incident_type_normalized, INCIDENT_BASE_PAYOUT["other"])

    if damage_estimate is not None:
        if damage_estimate < 0:
            raise ClaimAdjustmentError("damage_estimate cannot be negative.")
        assessed_amount = min(damage_estimate, base_amount * 3)
    else:
        assessed_amount = base_amount

    liability_adjusted_amount = assessed_amount * (liability_percentage / 100.0)

    payout_amount = max(0.0, liability_adjusted_amount - deductible)

    adjustment_record = {
        "claim_id": claim_id,
        "policy_number": policy_number,
        "incident_type": incident_type_normalized,
        "base_amount": round(base_amount, 2),
        "damage_estimate": damage_estimate,
        "assessed_amount": round(assessed_amount, 2),
        "liability_percentage": liability_percentage,
        "deductible": round(deductible, 2),
        "approved_payout": round(payout_amount, 2),
        "status": "adjusted",
        "adjusted_at": datetime.utcnow().isoformat(),
        "claimant_name": claimant_name,
        "claimant_phone": claimant_phone,
        "claimant_email": claimant_email,
        "incident_location": {
            "street": incident_location_street,
            "city": incident_location_city,
            "state": incident_location_state,
        },
    }

    _ADJUSTMENT_RESULTS[claim_id] = adjustment_record

    if claim_id in _SUBMITTED_CLAIMS:
        _SUBMITTED_CLAIMS[claim_id]["status"] = "adjusted"

    return adjustment_record


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# 4. Payment
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

def pay_claim(
    claim_id: str,
    policy_number: str,
    incident_date: str,
    incident_type: str,
    incident_location_street: str,
    incident_location_city: str,
    incident_location_state: str,
    claimant_name: str,
    claimant_phone: str,
    claimant_email: str,
    payment_method: str = "direct_deposit",
) -> Dict[str, Any]:
    """
    Issue payment for an adjusted claim.

    Raises ClaimPaymentError if the claim has not been adjusted,
    has already been paid, or has a zero/negative payout.
    """
    adjustment = _ADJUSTMENT_RESULTS.get(claim_id)
    if adjustment is None:
        raise ClaimPaymentError(f"Claim '{claim_id}' has not been adjusted yet.")

    if claim_id in _PAYMENT_RESULTS and _PAYMENT_RESULTS[claim_id]["status"] == "paid":
        raise ClaimPaymentError(f"Claim '{claim_id}' has already been paid.")

    payout_amount = adjustment.get("approved_payout", 0.0)

    if payout_amount <= 0:
        raise ClaimPaymentError(
            f"Claim '{claim_id}' has no approved payout amount (${payout_amount:.2f}) "
            "and cannot be paid."
        )

    valid_payment_methods = {"direct_deposit", "check", "wire_transfer"}
    if payment_method not in valid_payment_methods:
        raise ClaimPaymentError(
            f"Invalid payment method '{payment_method}'. "
            f"Must be one of: {', '.join(valid_payment_methods)}."
        )

    transaction_id = f"PAY-{uuid.uuid4().hex[:12].upper()}"

    payment_record = {
        "claim_id": claim_id,
        "policy_number": policy_number,
        "transaction_id": transaction_id,
        "amount_paid": payout_amount,
        "payment_method": payment_method,
        "claimant_name": claimant_name,
        "claimant_email": claimant_email,
        "status": "paid",
        "paid_at": datetime.utcnow().isoformat(),
    }

    _PAYMENT_RESULTS[claim_id] = payment_record

    if claim_id in _SUBMITTED_CLAIMS:
        _SUBMITTED_CLAIMS[claim_id]["status"] = "paid"

    return payment_record


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Convenience lookup functions
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

def get_claim_status(claim_id: str) -> Dict[str, Any]:
    """Retrieve the full processing status of a claim across all stages."""
    submission = _SUBMITTED_CLAIMS.get(claim_id)
    if submission is None:
        raise ClaimError(f"No claim found with id '{claim_id}'.")

    return {
        "claim_id": claim_id,
        "submission": submission,
        "validation": _VALIDATION_RESULTS.get(claim_id),
        "adjustment": _ADJUSTMENT_RESULTS.get(claim_id),
        "payment": _PAYMENT_RESULTS.get(claim_id),
    }


def process_claim_end_to_end(
    policy_number: str,
    incident_date: str,
    incident_type: str,
    incident_location_street: str,
    incident_location_city: str,
    incident_location_state: str,
    claimant_name: str,
    claimant_phone: str,
    claimant_email: str,
    damage_estimate: Optional[float] = None,
    deductible: float = 500.00,
    liability_percentage: float = 100.0,
    payment_method: str = "direct_deposit",
) -> Dict[str, Any]:
    """
    Convenience function that runs a claim through submission, validation,
    adjustment, and payment in sequence, using the same claim information
    throughout. Returns the results from each stage.
    """
    submission_result = submit_claim(
        None,
        policy_number,
        incident_date,
        incident_type,
        incident_location_street,
        incident_location_city,
        incident_location_state,
        claimant_name,
        claimant_phone,
        claimant_email,
    )
    claim_id = submission_result["claim_id"]

    validation_result = validate_claim(
        claim_id,
        policy_number,
        incident_date,
        incident_type,
        incident_location_street,
        incident_location_city,
        incident_location_state,
        claimant_name,
        claimant_phone,
        claimant_email,
    )

    if not validation_result["is_valid"]:
        return {
            "claim_id": claim_id,
            "submission": submission_result,
            "validation": validation_result,
            "adjustment": None,
            "payment": None,
        }

    adjustment_result = adjust_claim(
        claim_id,
        policy_number,
        incident_date,
        incident_type,
        incident_location_street,
        incident_location_city,
        incident_location_state,
        claimant_name,
        claimant_phone,
        claimant_email,
        damage_estimate=damage_estimate,
        deductible=deductible,
        liability_percentage=liability_percentage,
    )

    payment_result = pay_claim(
        claim_id,
        policy_number,
        incident_date,
        incident_type,
        incident_location_street,
        incident_location_city,
        incident_location_state,
        claimant_name,
        claimant_phone,
        claimant_email,
        payment_method=payment_method,
    )

    return {
        "claim_id": claim_id,
        "submission": submission_result,
        "validation": validation_result,
        "adjustment": adjustment_result,
        "payment": payment_result,
    }

import os
import json
import csv
import sqlite3
import logging
import datetime
import statistics
from dataclasses import dataclass, field, asdict
from typing import Any, Callable, Dict, List, Optional, Tuple

try:
    import matplotlib
    matplotlib.use("Agg")
    import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
    _HAS_MATPLOTLIB = True
except ImportError:
    _HAS_MATPLOTLIB = False


logger = logging.getLogger("experiment_logger")
if not logger.handlers:
    logging.basicConfig(level=logging.INFO)


class SensorValidationError(Exception):
    """Raised when a sensor reading fails validation."""
    pass


@dataclass
class SensorReading:
    sensor_id: str
    raw_value: float
    calibrated_value: float
    unit: str
    timestamp: str
    valid: bool
    notes: Optional[str] = None


@dataclass
class ExperimentLog:
    experiment_id: str
    readings: List[SensorReading] = field(default_factory=list)
    metadata: Dict[str, Any] = field(default_factory=dict)


def log_experiment_data(
    experiment_id: str,
    sensor_data: Dict[str, List[float]],
    valid_ranges: Dict[str, Tuple[float, float]],
    calibration_functions: Optional[Dict[str, Callable[[float], float]]] = None,
    units: Optional[Dict[str, str]] = None,
    output_dir: str = "experiment_output",
    db_path: str = "research_database.db",
    metadata: Optional[Dict[str, Any]] = None,
    generate_plots: bool = True,
    on_invalid: str = "flag",
) -> ExperimentLog:
    """
    Capture, validate, calibrate, store, visualize, and export experiment sensor data.

    Parameters
    ----------
    experiment_id : str
        Unique identifier for the experiment run.
    sensor_data : dict
        Mapping of sensor_id -> list of raw sensor readings.
    valid_ranges : dict
        Mapping of sensor_id -> (min_value, max_value) acceptable range.
    calibration_functions : dict, optional
        Mapping of sensor_id -> function(raw_value) -> calibrated_value.
        If not provided for a sensor, raw value is used as calibrated value.
    units : dict, optional
        Mapping of sensor_id -> unit string.
    output_dir : str
        Directory to store plots, CSV exports, and logs.
    db_path : str
        Path to the SQLite research database.
    metadata : dict, optional
        Additional metadata to store with the experiment (e.g., operator, conditions).
    generate_plots : bool
        Whether to generate visualization plots per sensor.
    on_invalid : str
        Behavior for invalid readings: "flag" (keep but mark invalid),
        "drop" (exclude from stored/calibrated results), or "raise" (raise exception).

    Returns
    -------
    ExperimentLog
        Structured log of the experiment including all readings and metadata.
    """
    if on_invalid not in ("flag", "drop", "raise"):
        raise ValueError("on_invalid must be one of: 'flag', 'drop', 'raise'")

    os.makedirs(output_dir, exist_ok=True)

    calibration_functions = calibration_functions or {}
    units = units or {}
    metadata = metadata or {}

    experiment_log = ExperimentLog(experiment_id=experiment_id, metadata=metadata)

    logger.info("Starting experiment logging for '%s'", experiment_id)

    for sensor_id, readings in sensor_data.items():
        if sensor_id not in valid_ranges:
            logger.warning(
                "No valid range specified for sensor '%s'; skipping validation.", sensor_id
            )

        min_val, max_val = valid_ranges.get(sensor_id, (float("-inf"), float("inf")))
        calib_func = calibration_functions.get(sensor_id, lambda x: x)
        unit = units.get(sensor_id, "unitless")

        for raw_value in readings:
            timestamp = datetime.datetime.utcnow().isoformat()
            is_valid = True
            note = None

            try:
                numeric_value = float(raw_value)
            except (TypeError, ValueError):
                is_valid = False
                numeric_value = float("nan")
                note = f"Non-numeric raw value: {raw_value!r}"

            if is_valid and not (min_val <= numeric_value <= max_val):
                is_valid = False
                note = (
                    f"Value {numeric_value} outside valid range "
                    f"[{min_val}, {max_val}]"
                )

            if not is_valid:
                if on_invalid == "raise":
                    raise SensorValidationError(
                        f"Sensor '{sensor_id}' reading invalid: {note}"
                    )
                elif on_invalid == "drop":
                    logger.warning(
                        "Dropping invalid reading for sensor '%s': %s", sensor_id, note
                    )
                    continue
                else:
                    logger.warning(
                        "Flagging invalid reading for sensor '%s': %s", sensor_id, note
                    )

            try:
                calibrated_value = calib_func(numeric_value) if is_valid else float("nan")
            except Exception as exc:
                logger.error(
                    "Calibration function failed for sensor '%s': %s", sensor_id, exc
                )
                calibrated_value = float("nan")
                is_valid = False
                note = f"Calibration error: {exc}"

            reading = SensorReading(
                sensor_id=sensor_id,
                raw_value=numeric_value,
                calibrated_value=calibrated_value,
                unit=unit,
                timestamp=timestamp,
                valid=is_valid,
                notes=note,
            )
            experiment_log.readings.append(reading)

    _export_to_csv(experiment_log, output_dir)

    if generate_plots:
        _generate_visualizations(experiment_log, output_dir)

    _export_to_database(experiment_log, db_path)

    logger.info(
        "Experiment '%s' logging complete: %d readings processed.",
        experiment_id,
        len(experiment_log.readings),
    )

    return experiment_log


def _export_to_csv(experiment_log: ExperimentLog, output_dir: str) -> str:
    csv_path = os.path.join(
        output_dir, f"{experiment_log.experiment_id}_readings.csv"
    )
    fieldnames = [
        "sensor_id",
        "raw_value",
        "calibrated_value",
        "unit",
        "timestamp",
        "valid",
        "notes",
    ]
    try:
        with open(csv_path, "w", newline="") as f:
            writer = csv.DictWriter(f, fieldnames=fieldnames)
            writer.writeheader()
            for reading in experiment_log.readings:
                writer.writerow(asdict(reading))
        logger.info("Exported readings to CSV: %s", csv_path)
    except OSError as exc:
        logger.error("Failed to write CSV export: %s", exc)

    meta_path = os.path.join(
        output_dir, f"{experiment_log.experiment_id}_metadata.json"
    )
    try:
        with open(meta_path, "w") as f:
            json.dump(experiment_log.metadata, f, indent=2, default=str)
        logger.info("Exported metadata to JSON: %s", meta_path)
    except OSError as exc:
        logger.error("Failed to write metadata JSON: %s", exc)

    return csv_path


def _generate_visualizations(experiment_log: ExperimentLog, output_dir: str) -> None:
    if not _HAS_MATPLOTLIB:
        logger.warning("matplotlib not available; skipping visualization generation.")
        return

    sensor_groups: Dict[str, List[SensorReading]] = {}
    for reading in experiment_log.readings:
        sensor_groups.setdefault(reading.sensor_id, []).append(reading)

    for sensor_id, readings in sensor_groups.items():
        valid_readings = [r for r in readings if r.valid]
        if not valid_readings:
            logger.warning(
                "No valid readings to plot for sensor '%s'; skipping plot.", sensor_id
            )
            continue

        indices = list(range(len(valid_readings)))
        calibrated_values = [r.calibrated_value for r in valid_readings]
        unit = valid_readings[0].unit

        try:
            fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(8, 4.5))
            ax.plot(indices, calibrated_values, marker="o", linestyle="-")
            ax.set_title(f"Sensor: {sensor_id} ({experiment_log.experiment_id})")
            ax.set_xlabel("Reading Index")
            ax.set_ylabel(f"Calibrated Value ({unit})")
            ax.grid(True, alpha=0.3)

            if len(calibrated_values) > 1:
                mean_val = statistics.mean(calibrated_values)
                ax.axhline(mean_val, color="red", linestyle="--", alpha=0.6, label=f"Mean={mean_val:.3f}")
                ax.legend()

            fig.tight_layout()
            plot_path = os.path.join(
                output_dir, f"{experiment_log.experiment_id}_{sensor_id}_plot.png"
            )
            fig.savefig(plot_path)
            plt.close(fig)
            logger.info("Saved plot for sensor '%s': %s", sensor_id, plot_path)
        except Exception as exc:
            logger.error("Failed to generate plot for sensor '%s': %s", sensor_id, exc)


def _export_to_database(experiment_log: ExperimentLog, db_path: str) -> None:
    try:
        conn = sqlite3.connect(db_path)
        cursor = conn.cursor()

        cursor.execute(
            """
            CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS experiments (
                experiment_id TEXT PRIMARY KEY,
                metadata TEXT,
                created_at TEXT
            )
            """
        )

        cursor.execute(
            """
            CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS readings (
                id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY AUTOINCREMENT,
                experiment_id TEXT,
                sensor_id TEXT,
                raw_value REAL,
                calibrated_value REAL,
                unit TEXT,
                timestamp TEXT,
                valid INTEGER,
                notes TEXT,
                FOREIGN KEY (experiment_id) REFERENCES experiments(experiment_id)
            )
            """
        )

        cursor.execute(
            """
            INSERT OR REPLACE INTO experiments (experiment_id, metadata, created_at)
            VALUES (?, ?, ?)
            """,
            (
                experiment_log.experiment_id,
                json.dumps(experiment_log.metadata, default=str),
                datetime.datetime.utcnow().isoformat(),
            ),
        )

        cursor.execute(
            "DELETE FROM readings WHERE experiment_id = ?",
            (experiment_log.experiment_id,),
        )

        rows = [
            (
                experiment_log.experiment_id,
                r.sensor_id,
                r.raw_value,
                r.calibrated_value,
                r.unit,
                r.timestamp,
                int(r.valid),
                r.notes,
            )
            for r in experiment_log.readings
        ]

        cursor.executemany(
            """
            INSERT INTO readings
                (experiment_id, sensor_id, raw_value, calibrated_value, unit, timestamp, valid, notes)
            VALUES (?, ?, ?, ?, ?, ?, ?, ?)
            """,
            rows,
        )

        conn.commit()
        logger.info(
            "Exported %d readings for experiment '%s' to database: %s",
            len(rows),
            experiment_log.experiment_id,
            db_path,
        )
    except sqlite3.Error as exc:
        logger.error("Database export failed: %s", exc)
    finally:
        try:
            conn.close()
        except Exception:
            pass

) -> ExperimentLog:
    """
    Capture, validate, calibrate, store, visualize, and export experiment sensor data.

    Parameters
    ----------
    experiment_id : str
        Unique identifier for the experiment run.
    sensor_data : dict
        Mapping of sensor_id -> list of raw sensor readings.
    valid_ranges : dict
        Mapping of sensor_id -> (min_value, max_value) acceptable range.
    calibration_functions : dict, optional
        Mapping of sensor_id -> function(raw_value) -> calibrated_value.
        If not provided for a sensor, raw value is used as calibrated value.
    units : dict, optional
        Mapping of sensor_id -> unit string.
    output_dir : str
        Directory to store plots, CSV exports, and logs.
    db_path : str
        Path to the SQLite research database.
    metadata : dict, optional
        Additional metadata to store with the experiment (e.g., operator, conditions).
    generate_plots : bool
        Whether to generate visualization plots per sensor.
    on_invalid : str
        Behavior for invalid readings: "flag" (keep but mark invalid),
        "drop" (exclude from stored/calibrated results), or "raise" (raise exception).

    Returns
    -------
    ExperimentLog
        Structured log of the experiment including all readings and metadata.
    """
    if on_invalid not in ("flag", "drop", "raise"):
        raise ValueError("on_invalid must be one of: 'flag', 'drop', 'raise'")

    os.makedirs(output_dir, exist_ok=True)

    calibration_functions = calibration_functions or {}
    units = units or {}
    metadata = metadata or {}

    experiment_log = ExperimentLog(experiment_id=experiment_id, metadata=metadata)

    logger.info("Starting experiment logging for '%s'", experiment_id)

    for sensor_id, readings in sensor_data.items():
        if sensor_id not in valid_ranges:
            logger.warning(
                "No valid range specified for sensor '%s'; skipping validation.", sensor_id
            )

        min_val, max_val = valid_ranges.get(sensor_id, (float("-inf"), float("inf")))
        calib_func = calibration_functions.get(sensor_id, lambda x: x)
        unit = units.get(sensor_id, "unitless")

        for raw_value in readings:
            timestamp = datetime.datetime.utcnow().isoformat()
            is_valid = True
            note = None

            try:
                numeric_value = float(raw_value)
            except (TypeError, ValueError):
                is_valid = False
                numeric_value = float("nan")
                note = f"Non-numeric raw value: {raw_value!r}"

            if is_valid and not (min_val <= numeric_value <= max_val):
                is_valid = False
                note = (
                    f"Value {numeric_value} outside valid range "
                    f"[{min_val}, {max_val}]"
                )

            if not is_valid:
                if on_invalid == "raise":
                    raise SensorValidationError(
                        f"Sensor '{sensor_id}' reading invalid: {note}"
                    )
                elif on_invalid == "drop":
                    logger.warning(
                        "Dropping invalid reading for sensor '%s': %s", sensor_id, note
                    )
                    continue
                else:
                    logger.warning(
                        "Flagging invalid reading for sensor '%s': %s", sensor_id, note
                    )

            try:
                calibrated_value = calib_func(numeric_value) if is_valid else float("nan")
            except Exception as exc:
                logger.error(
                    "Calibration function failed for sensor '%s': %s", sensor_id, exc
                )
                calibrated_value = float("nan")
                is_valid = False
                note = f"Calibration error: {exc}"

            reading = SensorReading(
                sensor_id=sensor_id,
                raw_value=numeric_value,
                calibrated_value=calibrated_value,
                unit=unit,
                timestamp=timestamp,
                valid=is_valid,
                notes=note,
            )
            experiment_log.readings.append(reading)

    _export_to_csv(experiment_log, output_dir)

    if generate_plots:
        _generate_visualizations(experiment_log, output_dir)

    _export_to_database(experiment_log, db_path)

    logger.info(
        "Experiment '%s' logging complete: %d readings processed.",
        experiment_id,
        len(experiment_log.readings),
    )

    return experiment_log


def _export_to_csv(experiment_log: ExperimentLog, output_dir: str) -> str:
    csv_path = os.path.join(
        output_dir, f"{experiment_log.experiment_id}_readings.csv"
    )
    fieldnames = [
        "sensor_id",
        "raw_value",
        "calibrated_value",
        "unit",
        "timestamp",
        "valid",
        "notes",
    ]
    try:
        with open(csv_path, "w", newline="") as f:
            writer = csv.DictWriter(f, fieldnames=fieldnames)
            writer.writeheader()
            for reading in experiment_log.readings:
                writer.writerow(asdict(reading))
        logger.info("Exported readings to CSV: %s", csv_path)
    except OSError as exc:
        logger.error("Failed to write CSV export: %s", exc)

    meta_path = os.path.join(
        output_dir, f"{experiment_log.experiment_id}_metadata.json"
    )
    try:
        with open(meta_path, "w") as f:
            json.dump(experiment_log.metadata, f, indent=2, default=str)
        logger.info("Exported metadata to JSON: %s", meta_path)
    except OSError as exc:
        logger.error("Failed to write metadata JSON: %s", exc)

    return csv_path


def _generate_visualizations(experiment_log: ExperimentLog, output_dir: str) -> None:
    if not _HAS_MATPLOTLIB:
        logger.warning("matplotlib not available; skipping visualization generation.")
        return

    sensor_groups: Dict[str, List[SensorReading]] = {}
    for reading in experiment_log.readings:
        sensor_groups.setdefault(reading.sensor_id, []).append(reading)

    for sensor_id, readings in sensor_groups.items():
        valid_readings = [r for r in readings if r.valid]
        if not valid_readings:
            logger.warning(
                "No valid readings to plot for sensor '%s'; skipping plot.", sensor_id
            )
            continue

        indices = list(range(len(valid_readings)))
        calibrated_values = [r.calibrated_value for r in valid_readings]
        unit = valid_readings[0].unit

        try:
            fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(8, 4.5))
            ax.plot(indices, calibrated_values, marker="o", linestyle="-")
            ax.set_title(f"Sensor: {sensor_id} ({experiment_log.experiment_id})")
            ax.set_xlabel("Reading Index")
            ax.set_ylabel(f"Calibrated Value ({unit})")
            ax.grid(True, alpha=0.3)

            if len(calibrated_values) > 1:
                mean_val = statistics.mean(calibrated_values)
                ax.axhline(mean_val, color="red", linestyle="--", alpha=0.6, label=f"Mean={mean_val:.3f}")
                ax.legend()

            fig.tight_layout()
            plot_path = os.path.join(
                output_dir, f"{experiment_log.experiment_id}_{sensor_id}_plot.png"
            )
            fig.savefig(plot_path)
            plt.close(fig)
            logger.info("Saved plot for sensor '%s': %s", sensor_id, plot_path)
        except Exception as exc:
            logger.error("Failed to generate plot for sensor '%s': %s", sensor_id, exc)


def _export_to_database(experiment_log: ExperimentLog, db_path: str) -> None:
    try:
        conn = sqlite3.connect(db_path)
        cursor = conn.cursor()

        cursor.execute(
            """
            CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS experiments (
                experiment_id TEXT PRIMARY KEY,
                metadata TEXT,
                created_at TEXT
            )
            """
        )

        cursor.execute(
            """
            CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS readings (
                id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY AUTOINCREMENT,
                experiment_id TEXT,
                sensor_id TEXT,
                raw_value REAL,
                calibrated_value REAL,
                unit TEXT,
                timestamp TEXT,
                valid INTEGER,
                notes TEXT,
                FOREIGN KEY (experiment_id) REFERENCES experiments(experiment_id)
            )
            """
        )

        cursor.execute(
            """
            INSERT OR REPLACE INTO experiments (experiment_id, metadata, created_at)
            VALUES (?, ?, ?)
            """,
            (
                experiment_log.experiment_id,
                json.dumps(experiment_log.metadata, default=str),
                datetime.datetime.utcnow().isoformat(),
            ),
        )

        cursor.execute(
            "DELETE FROM readings WHERE experiment_id = ?",
            (experiment_log.experiment_id,),
        )

        rows = [
            (
                experiment_log.experiment_id,
                r.sensor_id,
                r.raw_value,
                r.calibrated_value,
                r.unit,
                r.timestamp,
                int(r.valid),
                r.notes,
            )
            for r in experiment_log.readings
        ]

        cursor.executemany(
            """
            INSERT INTO readings
                (experiment_id, sensor_id, raw_value, calibrated_value, unit, timestamp, valid, notes)
            VALUES (?, ?, ?, ?, ?, ?, ?, ?)
            """,
            rows,
        )

        conn.commit()
        logger.info(
            "Exported %d readings for experiment '%s' to database: %s",
            len(rows),
            experiment_log.experiment_id,
            db_path,
        )
    except sqlite3.Error as exc:
        logger.error("Database export failed: %s", exc)
    finally:
        try:
            conn.close()
        except Exception:
            pass

    except Exception as e:

        raise ProvisioningError(stage, str(e))

    # ---------- Final summary ----------
    result = {
        "user": user_record,

        "permissions": permission_record,
        "workspace": workspace_record,
        "invitation_token": invitation_token,
        "audit_trail": audit_trail,
    }

            raise ValueError("window must be >= 1")
        smoothed = []
        for i in range(len(data)):
            start = max(0, i - window + 1)
            chunk = data[start:i + 1]
            smoothed.append(sum(chunk) / len(chunk))
        return self.load_dataset(smoothed, new_dataset_name or f"{dataset_id}_smoothed")

    def apply_normalization(self, dataset_id, method="minmax", new_dataset_name=None):
        data = self.get_dataset(dataset_id)["data"]
        if not data:
            raise ValueError("Dataset is empty")
        if method == "minmax":
            lo, hi = min(data), max(data)
            span = hi - lo if hi != lo else 1.0
            normalized = [(x - lo) / span for x in data]
        elif method == "zscore":
            mean = statistics.mean(data)
            std = statistics.pstdev(data) or 1.0
            normalized = [(x - mean) / std for x in data]
        else:
            raise ValueError(f"Unknown normalization method: {method}")
        return self.load_dataset(normalized, new_dataset_name or f"{dataset_id}_normalized")

    def apply_fft(self, dataset_id, new_dataset_name=None):
        data = self.get_dataset(dataset_id)["data"]
        n = len(data)
        spectrum = []
        for k in range(n):
            real = sum(data[t] * math.cos(-2 * math.pi * k * t / n) for t in range(n))
            imag = sum(data[t] * math.sin(-2 * math.pi * k * t / n) for t in range(n))
            magnitude = math.sqrt(real ** 2 + imag ** 2)
            spectrum.append(magnitude)
        return self.load_dataset(spectrum, new_dataset_name or f"{dataset_id}_fft")

        data = self.get_dataset(dataset_id)["data"]

        filtered = [x for x in data if abs((x - mean) / std) <= threshold]

        stats = {

            "mean": statistics.mean(data),
            "median": statistics.median(data),

            "min": min(data),
            "max": max(data),
            "range": max(data) - min(data)
        }

    def correlation(self, dataset_id_x, dataset_id_y):
        x = self.get_dataset(dataset_id_x)["data"]
        y = self.get_dataset(dataset_id_y)["data"]
        n = min(len(x), len(y))
        x, y = x[:n], y[:n]
        if n < 2:
            return 0.0
        mean_x, mean_y = statistics.mean(x), statistics.mean(y)
        cov = sum((xi - mean_x) * (yi - mean_y) for xi, yi in zip(x, y))
        std_x = math.sqrt(sum((xi - mean_x) ** 2 for xi in x))
        std_y = math.sqrt(sum((yi - mean_y) ** 2 for yi in y))
        if std_x == 0 or std_y == 0:
            return 0.0
        return cov / (std_x * std_y)

    def t_test(self, dataset_id_a, dataset_id_b):
        a = self.get_dataset(dataset_id_a)["data"]
        b = self.get_dataset(dataset_id_b)["data"]
        mean_a, mean_b = statistics.mean(a), statistics.mean(b)
        var_a = statistics.variance(a) if len(a) > 1 else 0.0
        var_b = statistics.variance(b) if len(b) > 1 else 0.0
        n_a, n_b = len(a), len(b)
        pooled_se = math.sqrt(var_a / n_a + var_b / n_b) if n_a and n_b else 1e-9
        t_stat = (mean_a - mean_b) / pooled_se if pooled_se != 0 else 0.0
        df = n_a + n_b - 2
        return {"t_statistic": t_stat, "degrees_of_freedom": df,
                "mean_a": mean_a, "mean_b": mean_b}

    def linear_regression(self, dataset_id_x, dataset_id_y):
        x = self.get_dataset(dataset_id_x)["data"]
        y = self.get_dataset(dataset_id_y)["data"]
        n = min(len(x), len(y))
        x, y = x[:n], y[:n]
        if n < 2:
            raise ValueError("Not enough data points for regression")
        mean_x, mean_y = statistics.mean(x), statistics.mean(y)
        num = sum((xi - mean_x) * (yi - mean_y) for xi, yi in zip(x, y))
        den = sum((xi - mean_x) ** 2 for xi in x)
        slope = num / den if den != 0 else 0.0
        intercept = mean_y - slope * mean_x
        predictions = [slope * xi + intercept for xi in x]
        ss_res = sum((yi - pi) ** 2 for yi, pi in zip(y, predictions))
        ss_tot = sum((yi - mean_y) ** 2 for yi in y)
        r_squared = 1 - ss_res / ss_tot if ss_tot != 0 else 1.0
        return {"slope": slope, "intercept": intercept, "r_squared": r_squared}

        all_data = [x for g in groups for x in g]
        grand_mean = statistics.mean(all_data)
        ss_between = sum(len(g) * (statistics.mean(g) - grand_mean) ** 2 for g in groups)
        ss_within = sum(sum((x - statistics.mean(g)) ** 2 for x in g) for g in groups)
        df_between = len(groups) - 1
        df_within = len(all_data) - len(groups)
        ms_between = ss_between / df_between if df_between else 0.0
        ms_within = ss_within / df_within if df_within else 1e-9
        f_stat = ms_between / ms_within if ms_within != 0 else 0.0
        return {"f_statistic": f_stat, "df_between": df_between, "df_within": df_within}

    def kmeans_cluster(self, dataset_id, k=2, max_iter=100, model_name=None):
        data = self.get_dataset(dataset_id)["data"]
        if k > len(data):
            raise ValueError("k cannot exceed number of data points")

        centroids = random.sample(data, k)
        assignments = [0] * len(data)

        for _ in range(max_iter):
            new_assignments = []
            for x in data:
                distances = [abs(x - c) for c in centroids]
                new_assignments.append(distances.index(min(distances)))

            if new_assignments == assignments:
                break
            assignments = new_assignments

            new_centroids = []
            for cluster_idx in range(k):
                members = [data[i] for i in range(len(data)) if assignments[i] == cluster_idx]
                if members:
                    new_centroids.append(sum(members) / len(members))
                else:
                    new_centroids.append(centroids[cluster_idx])
            centroids = new_centroids

        model_id = self._new_id("model")
        self.models[model_id] = {
            "id": model_id,
            "name": model_name or model_id,
            "type": "kmeans",
            "params": {"centroids": centroids, "k": k},

        mse = sum((yi - pi) ** 2 for yi, pi in zip(y, predictions)) / len(y)

        step = max(1, len(data) // width)
        sampled = data[::step][:width]

        grid = [[" " for _ in range(len(sampled))] for _ in range(height)]
        for col, value in enumerate(sampled):
            row = int((value - lo) / span * (height - 1))
            row = height - 1 - row
            grid[row][col] = "*"

            lines.append(f"{bin_start:8.2f} | {'#' * bar_len} ({count})")

        if std_x == 0 or std_y == 0:
            return 0.0
        return cov / (std_x * std_y)

    def t_test(self, dataset_id_a, dataset_id_b):

        b = self.get_dataset(dataset_id_b)["data"]
        mean_a, mean_b = statistics.mean(a), statistics.mean(b)
        var_a = statistics.variance(a) if len(a) > 1 else 0.0
        var_b = statistics.variance(b) if len(b) > 1 else 0.0
        n_a, n_b = len(a), len(b)
        pooled_se = math.sqrt(var_a / n_a + var_b / n_b) if n_a and n_b else 1e-9
        t_stat = (mean_a - mean_b) / pooled_se if pooled_se != 0 else 0.0
        df = n_a + n_b - 2
        return {"t_statistic": t_stat, "degrees_of_freedom": df,

    def linear_regression(self, dataset_id_x, dataset_id_y):
        x = self.get_dataset(dataset_id_x)["data"]

        n = min(len(x), len(y))
        x, y = x[:n], y[:n]
        if n < 2:
            raise ValueError("Not enough data points for regression")
        mean_x, mean_y = statistics.mean(x), statistics.mean(y)
        num = sum((xi - mean_x) * (yi - mean_y) for xi, yi in zip(x, y))
        den = sum((xi - mean_x) ** 2 for xi in x)
        slope = num / den if den != 0 else 0.0
        intercept = mean_y - slope * mean_x
        predictions = [slope * xi + intercept for xi in x]
        ss_res = sum((yi - pi) ** 2 for yi, pi in zip(y, predictions))
        ss_tot = sum((yi - mean_y) ** 2 for yi in y)
        r_squared = 1 - ss_res / ss_tot if ss_tot != 0 else 1.0
        return {"slope": slope, "intercept": intercept, "r_squared": r_squared}

        all_data = [x for g in groups for x in g]
        grand_mean = statistics.mean(all_data)
        ss_between = sum(len(g) * (statistics.mean(g) - grand_mean) ** 2 for g in groups)
        ss_within = sum(sum((x - statistics.mean(g)) ** 2 for x in g) for g in groups)
        df_between = len(groups) - 1
        df_within = len(all_data) - len(groups)
        ms_between = ss_between / df_between if df_between else 0.0
        ms_within = ss_within / df_within if df_within else 1e-9
        f_stat = ms_between / ms_within if ms_within != 0 else 0.0
        return {"f_statistic": f_stat, "df_between": df_between, "df_within": df_within}

    def kmeans_cluster(self, dataset_id, k=2, max_iter=100, model_name=None):
        data = self.get_dataset(dataset_id)["data"]
        if k > len(data):
            raise ValueError("k cannot exceed number of data points")

        centroids = random.sample(data, k)
        assignments = [0] * len(data)

        for _ in range(max_iter):
            new_assignments = []
            for x in data:
                distances = [abs(x - c) for c in centroids]
                new_assignments.append(distances.index(min(distances)))

            if new_assignments == assignments:
                break
            assignments = new_assignments

            new_centroids = []
            for cluster_idx in range(k):
                members = [data[i] for i in range(len(data)) if assignments[i] == cluster_idx]
                if members:

                else:

            centroids = new_centroids

        self.models[model_id] = {

        data = self.get_dataset(dataset_id)["data"]
        if not data:

        lo, hi = min(data), max(data)
        span = hi - lo if hi != lo else 1.0
        step = max(1, len(data) // width)
        sampled = data[::step][:width]

        grid = [[" " for _ in range(len(sampled))] for _ in range(height)]
        for col, value in enumerate(sampled):
            row = int((value - lo) / span * (height - 1))
            row = height - 1 - row
            grid[row][col] = "*"

        lines = ["".join(row) for row in grid]
        plot = f"{title}\n" + "\n".join(lines)

            "figures": included_figures or list(self.figures.keys()),

                pub["status"] = "finalized"

                self._log(f"Publication {pub_id} finalized")

        pub = next((p for p in self.publications if p["id"] == pub_id), None)

        dataset,
